Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC

1. Parse the grid, caps, and action schema. Treat each instance as independent and use only its demonstrations. Infer output dimensions and a full mapping for roles, boundaries, direction, extent, and collisions; verify the rule against every pair before applying it. For periodic/diagonal patterns, derive an explicit coordinate rule (modulus, orientation, phase) and verify successive rows and columns. Never infer a stripe, translation, reflection, or fill rule from resemblance alone.
3. For line-completion puzzles, verify the exact completion geometry from demos: determine whether gaps are filled only between collinear endpoints, whether endpoints can be in separate segments, and whether existing markers interrupt or bound lines. Do not extrapolate every row/column between global extrema unless the demo establishes that.
4. Request a demo only if you can name at least two plausible rules and the predicted outputs that distinguish them; weigh this information against demo cost. After receiving it, explicitly eliminate or retain the alternatives. Avoid additional demos when the examples already establish a consistent rule or no specific distinction remains.
5. After an incorrect submission, reassess the whole mapping against all demos and identify the unsupported assumption. Do not repeat or tweak a failed candidate without evidence distinguishing the new rule. If still underdetermined, request a targeted demo while its expected value justifies the cost; do not burn submissions on near-identical guesses.
6. Before each action, check remaining caps and cost. Validate submitted dimensions and values, then output only the one action JSON. Request demos with the exact action; use finish only after the instance is over.
